newsitem.title: USA: U.S. backs Intertanko in Washington state case.
newsitem.headline: U.S. backs Intertanko in Washington state case.

text.p: The U.S. Justice Department filed a motion partially backing tanker owners in a lawsuit against Washington state, an attorney for the International Association of Independent Tanker Owners attorney said Friday.
Intertanko is appealing a U.S. district court decision that upheld oil spill prevention regulations in Washington state that are stricter than federal laws.
The group is pressing to ensure that individual states may not pre-empt the federal government's regulations.
"The programs Intertanko is defending are federal programs," said Intertanko's attorney Jonathan Benner with the lawfirm Eckert, Seamans.
The government said the appeals court should send the case back to the district court to review all the issues individually.

"This Court must rule on the preemptive effect of several federal statutes, Coast Guard regulations, various international conventions, and a specific bilateral agreement between the United States and Canada involving traffic in the Strait of Juan de Fuca," the Justice Department filing said.

"We believe tha certain of those (state) rules are preempted, and that a remand is necessary for the district court to examine the Washington rules individually under the appropriate analysis," the department said.

It requested extra time to file a brief in the case because it wanted to "make certain that the Government states a preemption position that is no more broad than necessary because there is also a substantial federal interest in pursuing partnerships with states in order to prevent damaging oil spills."
The government said it would be prepared to file a brief in the case by May 2.
